Explorer Of The Seas13:0023:00

Santorini Island (Greece) is among the most popular ports of call on Eastern Mediterranean/Aegean cruises. The island is in the Aegean Sea and is the southernmost of the Greek Cycladic Islands.

The island's largest town and principal port is Fira/Thira (locode GRJTR).

Santorini (aka Thera/Thira) covers a total area of approx 91 km2 (35 mi2) and has population around 15,000.

Santorini Island is essentially what remained after an enormous volcanic eruption which destroyed the earliest settlements on a formerly single isle, and created the geological caldera. A large central, rectangular lagoon, measuring about 12x7 km (7,5x4,3 mi), is surrounded by 300 m (980 ft) high cliffs on 3 sides. The depth of the caldera is 400 m (1312 ft), which makes it impossible for any but the biggest ships to anchor anywhere in the bay. A fisherman's harbour is located at Vlychada, on the southwestern coast. The principal port on the island is Athinios. Fira is the capital, clinging to the top of the cliff that looks down on the lagoon. 

Santorini is the most active volcanic centre in the South Aegean Volcanic Arc, but what remains today is mainly a water-filled caldera. The island's volcanic arc is approx 500 km (310 mi) long and 20-40 km (12-25 mi) wide. The region became volcanically active about 3–4 million years ago, but volcanism on Thera started about 2 million years ago via the extrusion of dacitic lavas from vents around Akrotiri.

The island is the site of one of the biggest volcanic eruptions in recorded history: the Minoan eruption (sometimes called the Thera eruption), which occurred around 3,600 years ago at the height of Minoan civilization. The eruption left a huge caldera surrounded by volcanic ash deposits and may have led to the collapse of Minoan civilization on Crete, 110 km (70 mi) to the south, via a gigantic tsunami. Another theory holds that the Thera eruption is the source of the Atlantis legend.

Santorini's primary industry is tourism. The other main source of wealth includes agriculture. In recent years, the island has been voted one of the most beautiful in the world. Santorini remains the home of a flourishing wine industry, which is based on the Assyrtiko grape variety. White varieties include Aidani and Athiri, whereas red ones include mandilaria and mavrotragano.

In October 2017, the Greek Government ordered the raising of the sunken cruise ship Sea Diamond. The vessel foundered (took on water and sank) in 2007, leaving 2 passengers missing and 1 presumed dead. The decision was made as the wreck posed a potential environmental risk and was deemed a hazard to shipping near the island. On April 5, 2007, the 143-m ship struck a volcanic reef. All of its 1600 passengers and crew were evacuated, except a 45-year-old male passenger (of French origin) and his teenage daughter, who probably drowned. The bodies were never found. For cruise ship accidents you can visit our CruiseMinus section.

Santorini is the most popular cruising destination of all Greek Isles. The peak season runs from July through August. The towns on the island are situated atop high cliffs and are looking over the caldera of an ancient volcano. Just off Santorini (within the flooded caldera) are two neighboring uninhabited small islands - Nea Kameni and Palea Kameni - visited on boat tours/shore excursions from Thira. Nea Kameni is popular for hiking (to the crater) and swimming in its hot springs.

The closest to the cruise port, Thira/Fira International Airport, is approx 6 km/4 mi from downtown.

In 2017, Santorini self-imposed a daily cruise passenger limit of 12000. In 2018, this limit was further pushed down to 8000 per day.

The island's cruise port schedule for 2018 listed 439 ship calls (409 in 2017). For season 2019, 592 calls were handled and ~870,000 passengers.

Following the COVID crisis, in 2022 Santorini handled 686 cruise ship visits, which number in 2023 increased to 753 (112 in June alone).

In August 2024, Santorini implemented regulations to manage the influx of cruise ship tourists, limiting their number at the dock to 500 at any given time. The measure aimed to alleviate congestion and improve the overall vacation experience. However, tourists arriving on larger ships experienced delays as water shuttle operations (ship-to-shore transfers), leading to longer wait times for disembarking or returning passengers. Additionally, the Santorini Port Authority prohibited cruise vessels from providing water stations at the dock so visitors are advised to bring their own water ashore.

Royal Beach Club Santorini

The Royal Beach Club Santorini project was announced in October 2025.

Officially opened/inaugurated on April 27th, 2026, this private island resort offers passengers arriving on RCG-owned ships (from the fleets of Royal Caribbean International/RCI, Celebrity, and Silversea) exclusive access to the facilities and amenities. Local visitors can also be accommodated when capacity allows.

The new land experience, part of the company's shore excursion packages (Ultimate Santorini Day), is provided through a day pass granting beach access, dining options, sun loungers with umbrellas, Wi-Fi connectivity, and a coastal ferry link with stops at Santorini's villages Oia and Fira.

The complex features shaded cabanas, sunbeds, and a resort-style swimming pool with a poolside bar and lounge.

Pricing for October 2026 sailings on Explorer of the Seas was at ~US$280 per adult and ~US$200 per child, with promotional rates occasionally reducing these figures.

Santorini Island cruise terminal

Cruise ships to Santorini Island dock (anchor) at Thira - port town on the western coast. The cruise port is a tender port (doesn’t have a passenger terminal). Cruise vessels anchor in the caldera and their passengers are tendered ashore to the Old Port in Fira (Skala) via local tender boats (called skunas). Cruise liners usually call on Santorini Island at 8 am and leave at 6 pm.

Cruise ship tourists can reach Fira Town by walking, by donkey or by cable car. Cable car and donkey rides are affordably priced. A cable car is available every 20 min. Donkey rides from the cruise tender dock take up to 30 min, almost the same as walking.

Note: All cruise ship tourists must utilize local water shuttles to reach the island, which can result in extended waiting periods, especially when multiple large ships are in port simultaneously. Upon arrival, most cruisers take the cable car to ascend to Fira. Alternatively, you can opt for the Karavolades Stairs to reach Fira, though the steep, slippery, and exposed path can be challenging, particularly in hot weather.

Since 2025, cruise ship tourists visiting the islands of Santorini and Mykonos are charged a EUR 20/USD 21 fee, while other island destinations are charged a lower fee (EUR 5/US$5).
